title: CLO Tips Mini-Class - Exporting 3D Format Files
description: CLO technical experts take you through a comprehensive guide on how to export 3D file formats: OBJ, FBX, glTF 2.0 (GLB), glTF 2.0 (GLTF), and provide a detailed explanation of the usage of each function! Start learning now!

Hello everyone, today I will introduce you to the export of OPT files.  
First of all, I will introduce the relevant settings for exporting OPT.  
In the main menu bar, you can export the completed file as OPT.  
If you only want to export some of the content, you can first select the required version, model, etc.  
Then click on the OPT selected below, and here select export OPT.  
Select the appropriate save location, enter the name, and click save.  
When the OPT window appears, let's take a look at the specific settings.  
The top three rows are the contents of the export selection, including the version, virtual model, postage, and copy.  
The square on the left can be freely selected, and the arrow symbol button on the right can be opened.  
Select a single target to save the content you just selected as a single object.  
Selecting multiple targets can be divided into multiple objects.  
The main difference between merge and unmerge is reflected in the seam line.  
The grid point of the seam line is exported as one point or exported separately.  
The thick option below can save the rendering thickness of the version.  
The common UV coordinates are selected and the UV images can be exported as well.  
No big deal here, and we will release a detailed UV image video in the future.  
Take a look at the hidden objects, for example, a hidden model.  
Selecting this option can also export the model.  
If it is not selected, the hidden model or version will not be exported.  
Insert internal images, export files, including internal lines and internal images.  
Here you can set the size of the object, you can change the unit and adjust the proportion.  
The axis conversion allows the file to rotate in the direction of the three axes.  
In the picture, it is the direction of the 3D space XYZ axis.  
After selecting to save the flag color, it will save each flag color as an object file.  
Save to the path in the original text, in fact, saves both the text and the object to the path selected at the beginning.  
Save with the text file will generate a compressed package in the path selected at the beginning.  
The compressed package contains object files and text images, etc.  
After connecting the color and text together, the color will merge into the text image.  
If the object file is to be used in the model software, use this option, which can store files other than the environment color and the environment image.  
Save the transparent image from the slow reflection image.  
When the material contains the transparent image, click on this option to save the transparent image.  
Even if you don't click on it, the transparent effect can be retained.  
There is only one separate transparent image.  
Save the Meta data and save the clothing pages, grid, physical properties, and sewage information as MetaDataXML.  
The main menu bar file export FBX can export the finished file as FBX. Click Save.  
The FBX window appears.  
Let's take a look at the data.  
When you export, you can choose whether you need a virtual model or not, and the menu can be set to exclude the model skeleton.  
The following settings are the same as the option to export ARP to the front.  
After selecting the scene and props, you can also save the scene and other elements.  
Model Action  
If the model has an action, you can choose to save it.  
Connect has recently launched a lot of new actions, which are welcome to download and use.  
Cache Animation MC  
You can save the recorded costume animation as storage data.  
There are two types of files:  
Cache Animation MC 2-key, the file is saved as 2-key and cannot be opened by the user.  
S-key, the file is saved as an openable file.  
FBX SDK  
It is recommended to use the default version, which is also the highest version 2020, and the higher version can be integrated downwards.  
Comparison  
As in the previous settings, the saved text image is a relative file path, only the saved text name is saved, and the saved text image path is not saved.  
Therefore, if the saved FBX and the file used in the text image are under the same path, the text image will automatically be linked.  
Cache Animation MC  
Saves the text image absolute file path, saving the text image path within the file as the text image path.  
If you change the path of the text image, the text image will not be able to be imported into the media, and the text image will be embedded in the FBX file.  
In this text image mode, even if the FBX text image path is moved, the text can be normally linked.  
Color and Principle  
When the color is applied to the principle, the color and the principle will merge and be saved.  
FBX files cannot contain all the data, principle pictures, and colors, so select the option to export the color information applied to the principle.  
Save the color as before.  
Select a few versions first, then click on the main menu to export the FBX file.  
You can see there is one more option in the window.  
Workspace  
Select the workspace.  
The selected version is combined with the selected version.  
Before exporting, select the corresponding version.  
Using this function can merge a few specific versions.  
Next to introduce  
Export GLTF2.0 GLB  
File export GLTF2.0  
Say GLB format here first.  
This part of the above setting is the same as the export option, a little overlap.  
Light line  
Except for the rendering light line, it can be exported together with the light.  
Costume animation  
Export costume animation data.  
The rest of the settings have been mentioned before, and I will not repeat them here.  
Finally, I will add another function.  
Select the transparent value on the metal roughness map, then an extra green map will be added.  
Select the transparent value on the metal roughness map, then an extra green map will be added.  
Select the transparent value on the metal roughness map, then an extra green map will be added.  
Next to introduce  
Export GLTF2.0 GLTF  
File export GLTF2.0

chunks.title: CLO Tips Mini-Class - Exporting 3D Format Files
chunks.content: ## Exporting OPT Files in CLO: Settings and Procedures This section explains the process and detailed settings for exporting OPT files in CLO, including selection options, export parameters, and file content management relevant to 3D garment data and virtual models. ### Exporting OPT Files: Procedure Overview - To export an OPT file, use the main menu bar and select the export option for OPT. - You can export the entire file or select specific content such as a particular version or model before exporting. - After selecting the desired content, click on **OPT Selected** and then **Export OPT**. - Choose the save location, enter the file name, and click **Save** to open the OPT export window. ### Export Selection and Object Management - The top three rows in the OPT export window allow you to select the version, virtual model, postage, and copy to export. - Checkboxes on the left allow flexible selection of content. - The arrow button on the right opens additional options: - **Single Target:** Saves all selected content as one object. - **Multiple Targets:** Exports content as separate objects. - The key difference between **merge** and **unmerge** options affects seam lines: - **Merge:** Seam line grid points are exported as a single point. - **Unmerge:** Seam line grid points are exported separately. ### Exporting Thickness, UV, and Hidden Objects - The **Thickness** option saves the rendering thickness of the garment version. - UV coordinates and UV images can also be exported; detailed UV image tutorials will be provided separately. - Hidden objects or models can be included in the export by selecting the **Hidden Objects** option. - If not selected, hidden models or versions are excluded from the export. ### Internal Images and Object Scaling - The **Insert Internal Images** option exports internal lines and images inside the garment. - Object size can be adjusted by changing units or proportions. - Axis conversion allows rotation of the file along the XYZ axes to match 3D space orientation. ### Additional Export Options - **Save Flag Color:** Exports each flag color as a separate object file. - **Save to Path in Original Text:** Saves both the text and object files to the initially selected path. - **Save with Text File:** Generates a compressed package containing object files, text, and images. - When color and text files are combined, colors merge into the text images. - To use the object file in modeling software, select this option to exclude environment color and images. - **Save Transparent Image:** Exports transparent images for materials with transparency; transparency effects are retained even if this is not selected. - **Save Meta Data:** Exports clothing pages, grids, physical properties, and sewage (seam) information in a MetaDataXML file. --- ## Exporting FBX Files: Settings and Key Features This section covers exporting FBX files from CLO, including model options, animations, file versioning, and texture path management critical for 3D asset workflows. ### Exporting FBX: Initial Setup - Use the main menu bar to select **Export FBX**.

chunks.content: - **Save Transparent Image:** Exports transparent images for materials with transparency; transparency effects are retained even if this is not selected. - **Save Meta Data:** Exports clothing pages, grids, physical properties, and sewage (seam) information in a MetaDataXML file. --- ## Exporting FBX Files: Settings and Key Features This section covers exporting FBX files from CLO, including model options, animations, file versioning, and texture path management critical for 3D asset workflows. ### Exporting FBX: Initial Setup - Use the main menu bar to select **Export FBX**. - After clicking **Save**, the FBX export window appears with various settings. - You can include or exclude the virtual model and model skeleton. - Scene elements and props can also be included in the export. ### Model Actions and Animation Cache - If the model contains actions, you can choose to save these animations. - CLO Connect offers downloadable new actions for use. - Animation caching options: - **Cache Animation MC 2-key:** Saves animation as a non-editable file. - **Cache Animation MC S-key:** Saves animation as an editable file. ### FBX SDK Version and Compatibility - The recommended FBX SDK version is the default, version 2020. - Higher versions offer downward compatibility with earlier software. ### Texture and Path Handling in FBX Exports - Texture paths in FBX exports can be saved as relative or absolute: - **Relative Path:** Only the texture file name is saved; the path is relative to the FBX file location. Textures link automatically if FBX and textures are in the same folder. - **Absolute Path (Cache Animation MC mode):** The full texture path is embedded. Moving the texture file breaks the link unless embedded in the FBX file. - Embedding textures in FBX ensures textures remain linked even if files are moved. ### Color and Principle Map Export - Colors applied to principle maps merge and save together. - FBX files cannot contain all principle map data and colors simultaneously, so an option exists to export the color information applied to the principle separately. - Multiple versions can be combined before export using the **Workspace** selection, allowing merging of specific versions. --- ## Exporting GLTF 2.0 and GLB Files: Settings and Features This section describes exporting 3D assets in GLTF 2.0 and GLB formats, focusing on overlapping options with OPT exports, animation support, lighting, and transparency handling. ### Exporting GLTF 2.0 / GLB: Basic Settings - Both GLB (binary) and GLTF (JSON + external resources) formats are supported. - Export settings largely overlap with OPT export options for consistency. - Options include exporting costume animation data and rendering light lines. - Costume animation export supports saving animation data similarly to FBX. ### Transparency and Metal Roughness Maps - Selecting the transparent value on the metal roughness map adds an additional green channel map. - This extra map enhances transparency rendering in GLTF/GLB materials. - Repeated emphasis on this transparency feature highlights its importance for realistic material effects.

chunks.title: CLO Tips Mini-Class - Exporting 3D Format Files
chunks.content: - Export settings largely overlap with OPT export options for consistency. - Options include exporting costume animation data and rendering light lines. - Costume animation export supports saving animation data similarly to FBX. ### Transparency and Metal Roughness Maps - Selecting the transparent value on the metal roughness map adds an additional green channel map. - This extra map enhances transparency rendering in GLTF/GLB materials. - Repeated emphasis on this transparency feature highlights its importance for realistic material effects. --- ## Summary of Export Format Use Cases and Recommendations - **OPT Files:** Best for exporting CLO-specific garment versions with internal details like thickness, UV maps, internal images, and metadata. Suitable for CLO workflows and internal garment editing. - **FBX Files:** Ideal for integration with external 3D modeling and animation software. Supports skeleton exclusion, animation caching, texture embedding, and multiple version merging. - **GLTF/GLB Files:** Focused on web and real-time rendering applications with support for animations, lighting, and advanced transparency via metal roughness maps. GLB format is a single binary file, while GLTF separates JSON and resources. --- This structured guide provides comprehensive information on exporting 3D garment files from CLO software, covering essential settings, file format differences, and best practices for managing textures, animations, and metadata during export.
